headline: Trump names Stephen Miller White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles, effective Mon Nov 9
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Trump Truth Social post, quoted verbatim] 'I am pleased to announce that Mr. Stephen Miller, the current Deputy Chief of Staff of the Trump Administration, and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026.
sources: President Donald Trump, Truth Social post Nov 6 (primary source); USA Today, The Times, Le Monde, Indian Express, WHRO
fault_line: Doubling down on the agenda voters just rejected -- or putting the most loyal enforcer in charge before the Iran endgame?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Trump Truth Social post, quoted verbatim] 'I am pleased to announce that Mr. Stephen Miller, the current Deputy Chief of Staff of the Trump Administration, and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026. Susie Wiles, who has done an outstanding job, will be moving over to the Trump Political Operation.' Miller, 41, architect of the immigration crackdown and deputy chief of staff for policy / homeland security adviser since Jan 2025, replaces Wiles, the first woman to hold the post. Daily Caller reports Wiles gave Trump her resignation Thursday night. USA Today notes Miller 'has been a driving force in Trump's muscular approach to foreign affairs and threats of intervention abroad' and that the move signals Trump 'isn't ready to retreat from his MAGA agenda, despite an incoming Democratic-controlled Congress.' Le Monde frames it as doubling down after the midterm rout. [CONTEXT] Announced three days after Republicans lost both chambers of Congress in the Nov 3 midterms; the NBC eight-week window for renewed major Iran operations (recorded 1700-04) runs against the January swearing-in of the new Congress -- Miller as chief of staff becomes the gatekeeper of what reaches Trump in that window. Zero mentions in any Nov 6 or Nov 7 scan -- genuinely missed until this hour.
sections.what_verified: Le Monde (T2) confirms; USA Today, The Times, Indian Express, WHRO, Daily Caller, The Statesman (no declared tier in the registry -- attribution only) all carry the same Truth Social quote and Nov 9 date.
sections.what_disputed: None on the appointment itself. Interpretation is contested: USA Today/Le Monde read it as doubling down after the midterm defeat; the White House frames it as continuity with a trusted adviser. Miller's foreign-policy role is asserted by USA Today ('driving force in muscular approach to foreign affairs'), not by an official statement.
sections.why_matters: Three days after losing Congress, Trump puts his most loyal hardliner in charge of the White House -- days before the eight-week Iran window. What does Miller's promotion mean for the war?
